implementationNotes.resize: observed live on mac-arm64 against a Windows Server 2019 host on 2026-10-16: the desktop followed the window (874x520 -> 654x410 -> 1054x610 -> 874x520, read inside Windows) in 0.41-0.62 s without reconnect or password prompt, also after a reconnect; also observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (OPC, Windows Server 2022, app r4 with helper r3, to a Windows Server 2019 target): maximizing and restoring the app window took the footer 858x487 -> 1454x783 -> 858x487 and the remote desktop with its taskbar followed each time, without a reconnect or a password prompt; Windows 11 not tested
implementationNotes.reconnect: observed live on mac-arm64: after a normal disconnect, after a cut connection and after a helper crash (SIGKILL), Hubungkan ulang showed the dialog with user@host:port, asked for the password again, replaced the closed tab (one tab), checked the pin and restored the same session; the same on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 after a helper kill and after a hard network cut through a loopback forwarder (app r4)
implementationNotes.clipboard: observed live on mac-arm64 against Windows Server 2019 on 2026-10-16: both directions (remote to local with CRLF turned into LF, local to remote with LF turned into CRLF and a non-ASCII character), clipboard off (nothing crosses), exactly 32768 characters pass and 40000 or 45000 are refused whole in both directions, a file on the remote clipboard does not reach the Mac, remote text is written only while the app window is active; tested through the console (clip, Get-Clipboard), not in Notepad or other editors; also observed from the Windows client (windows-x64, 2026-10-16, OPC Windows Server 2022 to a Windows Server 2019 target, app r4 with helper r3, console only): the two-way exchange of short test strings; clipboard off (both boxes unticked, nothing crossed in either direction, checked with marker strings); the 32 KiB limit in both directions (ASCII, so bytes equal characters): 32768 passes (measured as 32768 on the receiving side) and 32769 is refused whole (the receiving clipboard keeps its previous marker; local to remote also shows 'Teks clipboard melebihi 32 KiB dan tidak dibagikan ke remote.'); and a file drop list of C:\Windows\win.ini on the remote clipboard (confirmed by get-clipboard -format filedroplist in the target) does not reach OPC (the text marker stays and no file arrives). Not repeated on Windows: 40000 and 45000 byte texts, the 'only while the window is active' rule, one-direction-only opt-in, multi-line and non-ASCII text, Notepad or other editors. Repeated from the Windows client with app r6 and helper r4 (windows-x64, 2026-10-16, 20:31-20:57, same lab path, console only, both boxes ticked): short strings crossed in both directions (remote to local remoter6text, local to remote localr6text); 32768 characters passed in both directions (measured as 32768 on the receiving side); 32769 was refused whole in both directions (the receiving clipboard kept its marker: remotebefore on the target, marker2 on OPC; local to remote showed 'Teks clipboard melebihi 32 KiB dan tidak dibagikan ke remote.' in the left panel, remote to local gave no notice; a control showed the target's clipboard holding the 32769 characters while OPC kept marker2). The Mac-to-OPC link dropped three times during the run (the Mac's own network showed 50 % packet loss to its gateway), which cost time and one repeated attempt but did not affect the app or its RDP session. Also repeated with r6 later the same evening (21:46-22:32, same lab path, console only): clipboard off (both boxes unticked) crossed nothing in either direction (marker strings unchanged); a file drop list on the remote clipboard (c:\windows\win.ini) reached OPC as neither text nor file (the OPC marker stayed and Get-Clipboard -Format FileDropList printed nothing); 40000 and 45000 character texts were refused whole in both directions (local to remote with the same notice, remote to local silently; control: the target's clipboard held the 45000 characters while OPC kept its marker). Then (22:39-23:29, same lab path, console only, app r6 with helper r4) each direction was enabled ALONE in its own session: with only remote → local the remote text reached OPC and a local text was neither offered nor applied (the target kept its marker), and with only local → remote the local text reached the target and a remote text never reached OPC; multi-line and non-ASCII text (the native names of the fr-FR, ja-JP and ru-RU cultures, three lines, 17 + 8 + 16 characters) crossed intact in both directions (remote to local: LF line endings on OPC, compared with -eq; local to remote: CRLF in the target, 45 characters, compared with compare-object also with -casesensitive and three lines read back) and a surrogate pair (U+1F600, built from the numbers 55357 and 56832) survived local to remote (-ceq True). Not repeated with r6: Notepad or other editors (how an LF-only text looks there), a non-BMP character from remote to local, the 'only while the window is active' rule. Observed live afterwards on windows-x64 on 2026-10-18 (app r9 with helper r6 on OPC, direct to MSSQL-BRIDGE, only 'Remote → lokal' enabled): a surrogate pair (U+1F600, built from 55357 and 56832 and put on the target's clipboard with Set-Clipboard) reached the OPC clipboard intact (length 2, -ceq True), and a text copied in NOTEPAD on the target (a, the pair pasted with Ctrl+V, b, a line break, np-dua; Ctrl+A and Ctrl+C with the app window focused) arrived exactly as a + U+1F600 + b + LF + np-dua (length 11, -ceq True), so Notepad's CRLF became LF on the Windows client too (CRLF would be 12). Remote to local non-BMP had also been seen on 2026-10-17 (app r7, delaying forwarder). Still not seen: other editors, rich text, the 'only while the window is active' rule on Windows. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.clipboard_notepad_non_bmp_live_windows_x64_20261018.

implementationNotes.cancel: observed live on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-16 as a cancel at 'Menghubungkan' through a local forwarder to the lab endpoint with its data held back: 'Sesi ditutup' within 0.22 s, helper gone, reconnect offered; not a cancel in the middle of an NLA exchange against a answering server; also observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (OPC, app r3): the connection went to a temporary PowerShell TCP listener on the OPC loopback that accepted but never answered (no forwarder, nothing sent to the lab server), the tab showed 'Menghubungkan...' with Putuskan enabled, one click on Putuskan gave 'Sesi ditutup' within 2 s, rdp-bridge was no longer a process, the listener was stopped afterwards
implementationNotes.helper-crash: observed live on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-16: SIGKILL of the helper gave 'Proses koneksi berhenti.' at once, no helper left, and Hubungkan ulang recovered the session; also observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (OPC, Windows Server 2022, app r4 with helper r3, to a Windows Server 2019 target): stop-process -id on the helper's PID (TerminateProcess) turned the tab into 'Koneksi gagal — Proses koneksi berhenti.' within about 3 s, the last frame stayed, Hubungkan ulang became available, no rdp-bridge process was left, and Hubungkan ulang (password typed again by the owner, clipboard off) restored the session in the same single tab Repeated on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (19:23-19:27) with app r5 and helper r4 through the loopback forwarder: PID 13012 was killed, the tab read 'Koneksi gagal — Proses koneksi berhenti.' within about 4 s, no helper was left and Hubungkan ulang (password typed again by the owner) restored the same session in the same single tab.
implementationNotes.network-interruption: observed live on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-16 as a hard cut of the TCP connection through a local forwarder (failure shown at once, Hubungkan ulang restored the same console); a silent packet loss without reset was not tested live; also observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (OPC, Windows Server 2022, app r4 with helper r3, to the same target) through a loopback TCP forwarder (work/netcut-20261016/forwarder.mjs, started on the OPC and removed afterwards): a TCP reset of the live connection at 14:45:54 turned the tab into 'Koneksi gagal — Sesi gagal dibentuk atau terputus.' within about 3 s, no helper was left, nothing reconnected by itself, and Hubungkan ulang (password typed again by the owner) restored the same Windows session in the same tab (same open console and history); a silent loss without a reset and a real cable loss were not tested Repeated on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (19:26:19) with app r5 and helper r4 through the same forwarder: the reset gave 'Koneksi gagal — Sesi gagal dibentuk atau terputus.' within about 5 s, no helper was left, the forwarder logged no new connection and Hubungkan ulang restored the same session in the same tab. Silent stall (no reset) observed live on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-18 through the controller's loopback forwarder, which holds the bytes of both directions without closing anything and answers the helper's TCP keepalives itself, so it is NOT a real path loss: stalls of 10, 30, 60 and 180 s to MSSQL-BRIDGE left the status at Terhubung with one helper and the picture frozen (the remote clock stayed at 4:18 PM while the real time passed 4:20), a resize requested during the stall was held and was answered 352-370 ms after the release, and the Windows Server 2019 host kept the session. The app shows no stall indicator (the status stays Terhubung). Not a check, no status changed; a real path loss (FreeRDP's TCP keepalive on the real socket, estimated at about 11 s) and the Windows client remain untested. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.silent_stall_live_mac_arm64_20261018.
implementationNotes.two-sessions: NOT observed as isolated sessions (not in checks): on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (app r4) a second Hubungkan with the same account created a second tab (both labelled with the host) and for about a minute both tabs showed Terhubung with their own canvas and the target's logon notice; a click on OK in tab 1 changed only tab 1 and tab 2 kept its notice until its own OK, so input goes to the active tab's session only. After OK in tab 2 its canvas showed the same desktop that tab 1 had shown (the same open console with its history), i.e. the server attached the new connection to the user's existing session (consistent with single session per user, inferred, the server policy was not read), and tab 1 ended as 'Koneksi gagal — Proses koneksi berhenti.' with a black canvas; exactly one helper was left (no leak) and Putuskan on the surviving tab gave 'Sesi ditutup'. Isolation of two separate Windows sessions needs a second disposable account; the GUI loopback suite covers it only against the test server. With app r5 (observed live on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16, 18:52-19:02) the same attempt gave two tabs labelled '10.28.0.173' and '10.28.0.173 (2)' and, after OK in tab 2, tab 1 ended as 'Sesi ditutup — Sesi diputus dari sisi server (oleh administrator atau pengguna). (kode 0x00000001)' while tab 2 showed the same console and history: still a takeover, not two isolated sessions; see server-ended-session With app r6 (observed live on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16, 20:04-20:13) the same attempt ended tab 1 as 'Sesi ditutup — Sesi diputus dari sisi server (oleh administrator atau pengguna). (kode 0x00000001)' followed by the takeover hint naming tab 2 ('10.28.0.173 (2)'), while tab 2 showed the same console and history: again a takeover, not two isolated sessions; see server-ended-session. Update 2026-10-17 (review, nothing observed, no check added): the only required check missing on mac-arm64 and windows-x64 is two-sessions; for mac-arm64 MSSQL-BRIDGE plus OPC can serve as the two hosts (OPC enforces one session per user, fSingleSessionPerUser=1 read on 2026-10-17, so a Mac connection as administrator takes over the Windows App session of OPC); windows-x64 still needs a second disposable account; the live run was prepared but not started, see resize_clipboard_r2.acceptance_review_20261017 in outputs/RDP-BUILD-EVIDENCE.json. OBSERVED live afterwards on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-17 (18:37-19:48, the owner typing the passwords): two tabs in one window to two different hosts, MSSQL-BRIDGE (Windows Server 2019) and OPC (Windows Server 2022), both Terhubung with their own desktops and exactly one helper each; a line typed in one tab appeared only in that tab (both directions); Putuskan on one tab, a reconnect of one tab and a SIGKILL of one helper each left the other tab connected and typable. The check two-sessions is therefore recorded for mac-arm64 (the status stays lab-partial until the owner reviews the evidence); it used two hosts, not two accounts on one host (a same-account connection only takes over, and OPC enforces one session per user too: a Windows App connection ended the Mac tab with error info 1 at 19:26:20); windows-x64 still needs a second disposable account. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.two_sessions_run_mac_arm64 in outputs/RDP-BUILD-EVIDENCE.json. OBSERVED live afterwards on windows-x64 (2026-10-17 20:46 to 2026-10-18 06:00, the owner typing the passwords): the app r9 on OPC opened two tabs to MSSQL-BRIDGE with two accounts, administrator (the existing session) and rdp-uji2 (a disposable account the owner created), both Terhubung with their own desktops and one helper each (PIDs 5964 and 14208, later 7916); lines typed in one tab appeared only in that tab (both directions); Putuskan on one tab, a reconnect of that tab and a TerminateProcess of its helper each left the other tab connected and typable. The check two-sessions is therefore recorded for windows-x64 too (all 10 required checks); its status stays lab-partial (Windows 11 baseline not run) until the owner reviews. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.two_sessions_run_windows_x64. implementationNotes.server-ended-session: Observed live with the fix, with a different code than expected (not in checks). Observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (app r4): when the server ended a session (the same account connecting again took over the first tab) the tab showed only 'Koneksi gagal — Proses koneksi berhenti.'. Fixed for app r5 and helper r4 (2026-10-16, test first): after its loop the helper reads freerdp_error_info and reports closed with a reason and the code; reasons other-connection (error info 5), logoff (2 and 0xC), admin-disconnect (1 and 0xB), timeout (3 and 4), server-denied (7, 9 and 0xA) and server-closed (any other code); the tab shows 'Sesi ditutup — <reason in Indonesian> (kode 0x...)'. Verified against the loopback test server, which sends a real error-info PDU (native integration: nine codes, the helper reports closed with the reason and exits 0; GUI loopback: the status text for code 5) and in the unit tests. Observed live on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16, 18:52-19:02 (app r5 with helper r4, OPC to MSSQL-BRIDGE, Windows Server 2019): a second connection of the same account took over the session and the first tab read 'Sesi ditutup — Sesi diputus dari sisi server (oleh administrator atau pengguna). (kode 0x00000001)': this server sent error info 1 (RPC-initiated disconnect), not 5, so the text is the generic admin-disconnect one (clear about who ended the session, but it does not say that another connection took over); the codes for idle and logon timeouts and for an administrator logoff were not observed For app r6 (2026-10-16, test first; unit tests and the GUI loopback suite, then observed live) the tab the server ended also gets 'Kemungkinan tab “<label>”, yang baru menyambung ke host dan akun yang sama, mengambil alih sesi ini.' when another tab of the same window to the same host, port and user opened after it, is still alive and opened at most five minutes before the end (reasons other-connection, admin-disconnect and server-closed only). Observed live on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16, 20:04-20:13 (app r6 with helper r4, OPC to MSSQL-BRIDGE, Windows Server 2019): after OK on the notice of the second connection of the same account (about 20:08:10) tab 1 read 'Sesi ditutup — Sesi diputus dari sisi server (oleh administrator atau pengguna). (kode 0x00000001) Kemungkinan tab “10.28.0.173 (2)”, yang baru menyambung ke host dan akun yang sama, mengambil alih sesi ini.' and kept the hint after switching tabs and after tab 2 was ended; Putuskan on tab 2 gave a plain 'Sesi ditutup'. This is one takeover on one server and the hint is a guess from the other tab, not a statement from the server; a takeover that ends with another code and Hubungkan ulang after a takeover were not observed. Seen twice, unplanned (windows-x64, 2026-10-16, between about 21:56 and 22:15 and again between about 22:50 and 22:59, app r6 with helper r4, OPC to MSSQL-BRIDGE; the second time the connection had waited about 9 minutes for the owner's answer, the first time about 18 minutes): a fresh connection left at the target's logon notice, with no OK, while the owner's confirmation was awaited ended as 'Sesi ditutup — Server meng-logoff sesi ini. (kode 0x0000000c)' (error info 0xC, LOGOFF_BY_USER, mapped to logoff, no takeover hint as designed); the cause was not established (the policy was not read, and the end time is unknown), the Windows session survived (the next connection found the same console, both times) and Hubungkan ulang after it restored the same tab (both times). The idle and logon-timeout codes are still unseen. Hubungkan ulang after a takeover (error info 1) observed live on mac-arm64 on 2026-10-18 (app r9 sources, helper r6, direct to MSSQL-BRIDGE, two tabs of the same account): tab 2 took tab 1 over (tab 1: 'Sesi ditutup — Sesi diputus dari sisi server (oleh administrator atau pengguna). (kode 0x00000001) Kemungkinan tab “10.28.0.173 (2)” ...', Hubungkan ulang enabled); Hubungkan ulang on tab 1 asked for the password again, reconnected to the same Windows session (pixel-identical frame), the reconnected tab took its label back and went last, and it ended tab 2 with the same text naming “10.28.0.173”; nothing reconnected by itself in the following 10 s. Not seen from the Windows client. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.reconnect_after_takeover_live_mac_arm64_20261018.
implementationNotes.keyboard-coverage: FIXED for app r5 (2026-10-16, test first; unit tests and the loopback test server, then observed live on windows-x64 the same day, see the end of this note): src/protocols/rdp/view.ts now maps F1-F12 (59-68, 87, 88), CapsLock (58), NumLock (69) and the keypad under their own scancodes (keypad Enter 0x11c and keypad divide 0x135 are told apart by the extended flag), and a guard test requires every mapped key to have a scancode of its own. The gap before the fix, read from the old table and observed on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16 (app r4): the scancode table was a US-layout probe without those keys, so they were not forwarded: the minus key sent by the automation through Windows App did not reach the target console in the one line tested while letters, digits, space and Return did (confirmed later the same day with ReadKey on OPC: the automation's minus and period are keypad keys, VirtualKeyCode 109 and 110, which the old table did not map, while comma 188, backslash 220 and the apostrophe 222 are main keys and all arrive; a real keyboard's main-row minus and period were already in the table); workaround used for the live test: aliases without hyphens. Observed live on windows-x64 on 2026-10-16, 18:52-19:02 (app r5 with helper r4, OPC Windows Server 2022 to a Windows Server 2019 target, console only): in the console inside the app the automation's minus and period (the keypad keys) arrived ('echo a-b.c' typed and run printed 'a-b.c'); with ReadKey in the target F12 gave VirtualKeyCode 123, F10 121, F5 116 and F1 112 (all NumLockOn), F3 recalled the previous command and F7 opened the history popup, and the app did not reload, open anything or change; F11 did not arrive, but it does not reach the OPC session either (checked in the OPC's own PowerShell), so it is lost before the product; CapsLock, NumLock, the keypad digits, Enter and divide were not pressed live. OBSERVED LIVE AGAIN on 2026-10-17, 13:21-13:39 (app r7 through the delaying forwarder, 375 ms each way, nested console in the target, ReadKey in the target): Tab (9, and the completion of 'get-pro' to 'Get-Process'), forward Delete (46 with the extended flag; the automation's key name 'Delete' is the Mac's Backspace = 8, so that was not a product fault), F1-F10 and F12 (112-121 and 123, 11 of 11 in order), Alt alone and alt+letter chords (18, then the letter, with LeftAltPressed; the outer app's menu bar stayed passive), Ctrl+C (17 then 67; as an interrupt it stopped a running ping within 1 s, as copy it put the console selection on the OPC clipboard), shift+Tab (16, 9), Down 40, PageUp 33 and PageDown 34 (extended) all arrived correctly and in order at a round trip of 0.75 s; NOT tried: Alt+Space (the Raycast hotkey on the owner's Mac, so it cannot be tested through the automation), Alt+Tab, held-key repeat, AltGr, IME, F11, Insert, CapsLock, NumLock and the keypad digits

implementationNotes.x86_64-rosetta-live: observed live from the Mac on 2026-10-16/17 for the x86_64 r4 helper run through Rosetta (arm64 host, arm64 Electron; NOT a physical Intel Mac, so mac-x86_64 stays fixture-tested and no check is added): login to MSSQL-BRIDGE with the verified pin and NLA, keyboard input through the guarded controller, window resize (the canvas followed to 654x410, 1054x610 and 874x520 and Windows reported the same primary monitor size) and the text clipboard in both directions with 32768 characters passing and 32769 refused whole each way and a file reference ignored (an in-memory Mac clipboard was used, so the real macOS pasteboard path was not exercised with this helper). The first attempt failed with 0x0002001c (ERRCONNECT_ACTIVATION_TIMEOUT) because the Mac's round-trip time to the lab network was about 2 s while FreeRDP waits 9 s for the whole post-security sequence; a loopback sweep with a delaying forwarder shows the x86_64 and arm64 helpers behave identically (they connect up to 1.6 s and fail from 1.8 s). Not observed with this helper: helper-crash, network-interruption, wrong-credentials, certificate-mismatch, cancel, clipboard off, 40000/45000 characters, one direction only, multi-line and non-ASCII text. OBSERVED afterwards on 2026-10-18 with the x86_64 r6 helper (sha256 f7aa3cff5a6f..., a staged app tree with the arm64 Electron and the app r9 sources; the helper process maps the Rosetta runtime) against the real Windows Server 2019: certificate-mismatch (a wrong pin, fictitious user, blank password: 'Sertifikat tidak dipercaya atau pin tidak sesuai (kode 0x00020008)' 837 ms after 'Menghubungkan'), cancel (a held-back connection through the controller's forwarder: 'Sesi ditutup' 69 ms after the click, helper gone), wrong-credentials (fictitious user and an arbitrary password typed by the owner: 'Autentikasi ditolak (kode 0x00020014)', one failed logon, no retry), helper-crash (SIGKILL: 'Proses koneksi berhenti.' in 201 ms at the logon notice and 220 ms on an established session, Hubungkan ulang restored the same desktop after the first) and network-interruption (a hard TCP cut: 'Sesi gagal dibentuk atau terputus.' in 178 ms, no automatic reconnect, Hubungkan ulang restored the same desktop). Still not observed with this helper: two-sessions, the clipboard variants, a physical Intel Mac or Electron x64; mac-x86_64 stays fixture-tested and no check was added. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.x86_64_rosetta_remaining_checks_live_20261018.
implementationNotes.slow-path-message: Not an acceptance check (no check added, no platform status changed). Added 2026-10-17, test first, at the owner's request after the live x86_64 attempt: the renderer now words error 0x0002001c (ERRCONNECT_ACTIVATION_TIMEOUT, reason 'connection') as 'Jaringan atau server terlalu lambat: sesi tidak selesai dibentuk dalam batas waktu. Coba lagi saat jaringan lebih cepat.' (status line 'Koneksi gagal — … (kode 0x0002001c)'); every other reason and code keeps its text. Covered by unit tests (reasonText) and loopback GUI scenario 15 (real app, real helper and a delaying loopback forwarder: 150 ms each way connects, 1200 ms each way ends with the new text). No timeout was changed (FreeRDP's 9 s TcpAckTimeout window and the owner's 30 s deadline). In the Windows r7 package (built 2026-10-17; harness and --fixture on OPC the same night; not in the r6 package). OBSERVED LIVE on windows-x64 on 2026-10-17 07:38-07:39 (OPC to MSSQL-BRIDGE through a loopback forwarder that delays every chunk 1000 ms each way, round trip 2 s): after 16.1 s the tab read 'Koneksi gagal — Jaringan atau server terlalu lambat: sesi tidak selesai dibentuk dalam batas waktu. Coba lagi saat jaringan lebih cepat. (kode 0x0002001c)', while the control path (100 ms each way) connected normally. The slow path is simulated by the local forwarder, not a real slow network. RTT THRESHOLD of MSSQL-BRIDGE measured live on 2026-10-17 08:36-08:58 with forwarder r2 from OPC (one attempt per point): it connects at 300 ms and 375 ms each way (round trip 0.6 s and 0.75 s) and ends with the same text and code at 450 ms (0.9 s, after 11.9 s), 600 ms (1.2 s, after 13.3 s) and, earlier, 1000 ms (2.0 s, after 16.1 s), so the threshold lies between a round trip of 0.75 s and 0.9 s (the loopback test server connects up to 1.6 s and fails from 1.8 s). HUBUNGKAN ULANG after such a failure was also observed live on OPC the same morning (09:16-09:21, forwarder r2 on port 4329): after the 450 ms failure (0x0002001c, reproduced a second time with identical byte counts) the button stayed enabled, it opened the same credential dialog for the same target with the same clipboard setting and an empty password, and after the forwarder on that port was swapped to 100 ms each way the reconnect connected in the SAME tab and replaced the failure text. USE OF A SLOW BUT WORKING PATH was observed live too (10:42-10:50, forwarder r2, 375 ms each way = round trip 0.75 s, both clipboard directions ticked): maximizing and restoring the window made the remote desktop follow in about 2-3 s (858x487 <-> 1454x783) without reconnect or password prompt, a key echoed in about 1-1.5 s, a 42-character burst arrived complete and in order, text clipboard sync worked in both directions, and the session stayed up 7 min 57 s; the 375 ms point connected twice (08:57, 10:42) and 450 ms failed twice (08:55, 09:16). A connection left at the target's logon notice was ended by the server with 0x0000000c after 2 min 14 s. THE THRESHOLD WAS NARROWED the same morning (11:07-11:10, forwarder r2): 400 ms (round trip 0.8 s) and 425 ms (0.85 s) each way both connected (one sample each), so with 450 ms failing twice the threshold of MSSQL-BRIDGE lies between a round trip of 0.85 s and 0.9 s (about 10 round trips fit in the 9 s window if the server's own time is ignored, against about 5 for the loopback test server). THE BOUNDARY WAS REPEATED at 12:47-12:55 (forwarder r2): 425 ms each way (0.85 s) connected again (2 of 2) and 450 ms each way (0.9 s) failed again with the same text and code (3 of 3), the three failures identical in the forwarder log (3557 B up, 2724 B down, 11.85-11.90 s), so the threshold of MSSQL-BRIDGE is confirmed between a round trip of 0.85 s and 0.9 s. KEYS AND LARGE CLIPBOARD on the same slow path (375 ms each way, 11:28-11:43, one 15-minute session, both clipboard boxes ticked): shifted letters, the shifted digit symbols, punctuation (: ; , . - | \ " ' < ~ `), BackSpace/Home/Right/End and Ctrl+V all arrived correctly with no stuck Shift ('>' cannot be typed with the tool: shift+period gives '.'); a 32768 byte text crossed both ways complete (local to remote read in the target within about 3 s of the paste; remote to local within about 4.5 s), and a 40000 byte text was refused both ways (local to remote with the red notice 'Teks clipboard melebihi 32 KiB dan tidak dibagikan ke remote.' shown for about 6 s), the session staying up. NON-ASCII, MULTI-LINE AND MOUSE DRAG on the same slow path (375 ms each way, 12:08-12:23, one 15-minute session, both clipboard boxes ticked): three culture names in French, Japanese and Cyrillic (built with new-object ... .nativename, 17+8+16 characters) crossed intact in both directions (case-sensitive comparison on both sides; LF line endings in the OPC clipboard, CRLF in the target's), a non-BMP character (U+1F600, built from two surrogate numbers) crossed remote to local intact (and twice local to remote), and mouse drags on the canvas worked: a drag-selection in the target's console highlighted about 1 s after the release, was copied with Enter and reached the OPC clipboard (19, 71 and 51 characters for a one-line, a diagonal and a released-outside-the-canvas drag), with no button left pressed after a release outside the canvas.
implementationNotes.mouse-wheel: IMPLEMENTED after the live finding described here (2026-10-17, test first; app r8 and helper r5; seen on loopback macOS and, on OPC (2026-10-17), in two steps: 15:03-15:06 as the Windows helper r5 and its new unit test control-test.exe passed through the harness and 30 wheel turns over the --fixture canvas did not end the session; then LIVE at 15:26-15:30 against MSSQL-BRIDGE (app r8 + helper r5, direct connection, the owner typed the password): the wheel scrolled the target's PowerShell console by 3 lines per notch, up and down, at the position under the pointer (a wheel over the target's empty taskbar did not scroll it), see resize_clipboard_r2.mouse_wheel_r8.opc_live_wheel; not in checks, no platform status changed). The gap before the fix (app r7, found 2026-10-17, 13:28-13:30, OPC to MSSQL-BRIDGE through the delaying forwarder at 375 ms each way): the canvas has no wheel listener (src/desktop/renderer.ts:19-23), the Input type of src/protocols/rdp/wire.ts has no wheel input and native/rdp/bridge.cpp:155-161 never sends a wheel flag; live, scrolling up 5 and then 10 wheel ticks over the canvas did not move the target console (172..200 stayed on top after printing 1..200) while the same automation wheel scrolled the app's own left panel, so the wheel reaches the app and is dropped by it. Mac trackpad scrolling would do nothing in a remote window. To implement (test first): a wheel input in the wire format with validation, a renderer wheel handler using the canvas bounds and the delta, PTR_FLAGS_WHEEL (with PTR_FLAGS_WHEEL_NEGATIVE) in the helper, a loopback test-server check and then a live check; horizontal wheel, Ctrl+wheel and trackpad inertia only afterwards. Evidence of the finding: resize_clipboard_r2.delay_forwarder.opc_live_other_keys_wheel in outputs/RDP-BUILD-EVIDENCE.json. THE FIX: wire.ts (a wheel input, WHEEL_LIMIT 4800), view.ts (wheelUnits and makeInputState().wheel with a carried fraction), renderer.ts (a non-passive wheel listener on the canvas), control.hpp (validate_control, wheel_steps, wheel_flags) and bridge.cpp (move the pointer, then the wheel events, at most 255 units each); checked by 5 new unit tests, the C++ control test, a loopback integration scenario against the real helper and the FreeRDP test server (arm64 and x86_64 helpers), a GUI loopback scenario (it FAILS on the r7 package and passes on r8) and 25 mutants (all killed); the app package r8 and the helper package channels-r5 were built, run on OPC through the harness and --fixture (resize_clipboard_r2.mouse_wheel_r8.opc_run) and then used in that live run. A helper r4 or older refuses the wheel control and ends the session on the first wheel turn, so the app and the helper must be paired. Horizontal wheel and Ctrl+wheel were implemented afterwards (app r9, helper r6; see horizontal-wheel-and-pinch). Still missing: tuning for trackpad inertia (no real trackpad was used), windows other than a console, and single wheel events larger than one notch (the automation sends one notch per action). Evidence of the fix: resize_clipboard_r2.mouse_wheel_r8 in outputs/RDP-BUILD-EVIDENCE.json.
implementationNotes.horizontal-wheel-and-pinch: IMPLEMENTED on loopback (2026-10-17, test first; app r9 and helper r6) and afterwards run on OPC through the harness and --fixture only (17:19-17:33: the Windows r6 helper and control-test.exe with the hwheel assertions passed, and 32 wheel ticks, vertical and horizontal, over the --fixture canvas left the tab Terhubung; the fixture helper ignores them, so this shows only that the session was not ended), and then run LIVE once against MSSQL-BRIDGE from OPC (17 Oct 17:41-17:59: the horizontal wheel worked, see Live result below); not in checks, no platform status changed. After the live wheel run, which showed the vertical wheel working on Windows, app r8 still dropped deltaX and a pinch (a Mac trackpad pinch reaches the page as a wheel event with ctrlKey and no Ctrl key press, so the remote never saw Ctrl). THE FIX: a control type hwheel ({type:'hwheel',x,y,delta}: the shape and limits of wheel, positive = to the right as WM_MOUSEHWHEEL; a type of its own on purpose, because a helper r5 ignores unknown fields and would have scrolled a sideways turn vertically, while an unknown type is refused loudly), wire.ts (the type), view.ts (hwheelUnits, a carried fraction per axis, and Ctrl pressed around a turn that arrives with ctrlKey unless the user already holds Ctrl: one press and release per turn, nothing kept between turns), renderer.ts (deltaX and ctrlKey are forwarded with the wheel), control.hpp (validate_control, wheel_flags(step,horizontal): flag 0x0400 plus the 9-bit count) and bridge.cpp (one branch for both axes). FreeRDP drops PTR_FLAGS_HWHEEL events silently when the server did not announce horizontal wheel support (it overwrites its own setting with the server's capability), which a new --no-hwheel option of the loopback test server shows: nothing is sent, the session carries on. Checked by 7 new unit tests (78 of 78), the C++ control test, 3 new integration scenarios against the real helper (15 for arm64 r6 and x86_64 r6), 2 new GUI loopback scenarios (18 of 18 on the r9 package; both FAIL on the r8 package) and 54 mutants (all killed). App and helper must be paired: a helper r5 or older ends the session with control-protocol on the first hwheel. Live result (17 Oct 17:41-17:59, OPC -> MSSQL-BRIDGE directly, app r9 + helper r6, clipboard off, the owner typed the password and clicked OK on the logon notice): in the target's nested PowerShell console, widened to a 300-column buffer with a ruler line on screen, each scroll action of the tool to the RIGHT moved the view 3 columns to the right (the content to the left), each one to the LEFT 3 columns back, stopping at column 0; 5 actions 0.3 s apart gave exactly 15 columns (no tick lost) and scroll_amount 5 was still one notch; the vertical wheel still worked (2 up = 6 lines, 2 down = 6 lines back). So MSSQL-BRIDGE announces horizontal wheel support, the direction (right = positive) is right, the Windows App forwards the Mac's horizontal scroll, and the app turns it into hwheel (an inference: no negative control was run). Still not seen: the Ctrl pinch (the Ctrl bracket) live, the r9 app with a helper r5 on Windows (and r8, the other negative control), other lab hosts, a real trackpad (a real pinch, inertia, fractional deltas, events larger than one notch), a window other than a console, side effects of a Ctrl tap on a real remote. Evidence: resize_clipboard_r2.hwheel_ctrl_r9 (opc_live_hwheel) in outputs/RDP-BUILD-EVIDENCE.json.
implementationNotes.close-finished-tab: Not an acceptance check (no check added, no platform status changed).
